messages:
sam: Heads-up — since this morning we've seen gRPC streaming stalls on GPU jobs between pods on node-pair us-west2-b (nodeA <-> nodeB). ~30% of streams hit a hang during long-running model shards.
maya: Any error patterns? logs?
sam: gRPC streams stop making progress, TCP stays ESTABLISHED, throughput drops to ~0. No retries from client for ~30s, then reconnect. Stack traces show kernel-level retransmit/fragment issues.
oliver: Could be MTU or encap. We recently bumped Geneve MTU for bigger batches.
raj: I grabbed tcpdump on nodeA->nodeB during a stall. Noticed lots of 'Fragmented IP' and retries. Also some ICMP msgs: "fragmentation needed, DF set" from intermediate overlay.
maya: Can you paste the tcpdump snippet?
raj: ```
09:21:13.123456 IP hostA > hostB: Flags [P.], seq 12345:22345, ack 34567, win 64240
09:21:13.123460 IP (frag 1) hostA > hostB: GRE
09:21:13.123470 ICMP hostB > hostA: frag needed and DF set, mtu 1450
```
sam: Thanks. Node MTU is 9000, geneve overlay carried an extra 50 bytes; but the HW VF on some nodes (SR-IOV) advertises 1450. Looks like a mismatch between VF representor, host bridge, and CNI mtus.
tess: Which nodes are SR-IOV? Are they evenly distributed?
sam: NodeB and a subset of GPU nodes are SR-IOV attached NICs with firmware that clamps VF MTU to 1450 in older driver. NodeA is standard VNET with 9000. The path hits a node with VF->bridge->geneve translation and drops/ICMPs.
oliver: That explains fragmentation and gRPC stalling: gRPC uses long streaming frames and suffers when IP fragments are dropped or reordered. The runtime's continuous batching means single token sequences exceed path MTU once kernel offload strips headers differently.
maya: Workaround we tested on a pod: `ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1400` inside container — streaming recovered. But that's not scalable.
raj: On-node quick fix we applied: set VF MTU to 8900 on affected nodes (temporary) and disabled GSO/TSO on representative ports where driver misbehaved: `ethtool -K ethX tso off gso off gro off` — streams resumed.
tess: Any perf tradeoffs turning off GSO/TSO?
raj: CPU use increased slightly (~8-12%) on the NIC host during heavy token generation but much better than job failures.
sam: Proposed rollout plan: 1) identify all nodes with SF-IOV VF driver version < 2.3 and schedule kernel/firmware upgrade; 2) patch CNI to clamp overlay MTU to min-path-MTU at setup time; 3) add node-level readiness probe that validates VF/bridge MTU alignment; 4) short-term: k8s DaemonSet to `ethtool -K ... off` on flagged nodes during business hours.
maya: +1 on clamp at CNI — we should always compute safe MTU from underlying device and overlay overhead.
raj: I can script a check to run in CI that detects mismatched MTU between `ip link show` on host and `ip link show` in container netns and fail the node as NotReady if mismatch > 200 bytes.
oliver: Also add a runtime mitigation: make gRPC streaming detect persistent path-DF ICMPs for a stream and convert to smaller chunking (server-side chunk cap) to avoid single-frame fragmentation. That reduces throughput slightly but keeps sessions alive.
sam: Good idea — can the runtime change be toggled via config flag per nodepool?
oliver: Yes, we can gate by nodepool label and roll it via Dedicated config. Will open PR.
tess: Any security/ops concerns with disabling offloads?
raj: Need to notify networking team — offloads are preferred; long-term should be driver+firmware fix. Disabling is emergency-only.
sam: Action items: @raj to inventory SR-IOV nodes and deploy ethtool DaemonSet (ASAP). @maya to coordinate CNI patch and rollout window. @oliver to open runtime PR for chunking fallback. I'll schedule a node upgrade wave for firmware/driver next week and post ETA.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0318-01 - "podstream-throttle-mtu-encap-mismatch" (priority: high)
maya: Thanks. I'll post the CNI patch link when ready. Also adding a probe to Console to surface per-route DF ICMP counts so SREs can detect early.
sam: Perfect. Keep updates here. If anyone finds a node still flaking after ethtool patch, ping me and include `sudo ip -d link show` and `dmesg | grep -i frag` output.
raj: Will do. For reference, debug commands we used: ```
# host: check phys dev mtu
ip link show | grep -E "eth|ens"
# container: check container ns mtu
nsenter -t $(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Pid}}' $CID) -n ip link show eth0
# capture broken path
tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w /tmp/frag.pcap host <peer-ip>
```
maya: Copy. Closing loop after CNI patch + ethtool rollout validated. :thumbsup:
